Scope semantic caches to one turn

PR 127 · 6 files · +391 / −67

ONE WAY IN

Six trays.
One closing routine.

Picture a TypeScript workbench with six trays of reusable answers. The specialist still does the work. A reusable organizer now owns the trays’ clearing routine. Wiping the trays and finishing the workshop’s shutdown are separate moments.

The specialist keeps the tools
Six trays keep different kinds of answers apart.
The organizer empties the trays
Previously stored answers stop being available immediately.
The supervisor waits for shutdown
Only then does the closing call finish or report failure.

Core supplies the organizer; each TypeScript query service owns one. The backend waits for project cleanup. A fresh work session starts only after refresh succeeds.

Metaphor: trays are caches, not work queues. Emptying them neither cancels work nor closes access to a cleared tray afterward.

01 / THE WHOLE CHANGE

Six stores stay separate.
Their lifetime gets one owner.

TypeScript still computes the answers. Core supplies the cache mechanism. The backend now waits for project release.

04 / LOOKUP · D3–D4

A promise is the cached value.
The scope never waits for it.
↑ D3: values
↑ D4: failures
Key is already present
Map.has(key) is true.
Return Map.get(key) exactly.
Do not call the factory.

Applies to an empty array, an explicit undefined, or a promise that has rejected.

Key is absent
Call the factory synchronously.
If it returns, insert that exact value.
If it throws, insertion is never reached.

A returned promise is inserted immediately. A thrown error leaves no entry, so the next lookup retries.

STATED · D3–D4

The PR explicitly preserves value/promise identity and failure behavior. Its reason for Map.has is that undefined can itself be a cached value.

FACTORY BEHAVIOR	SECOND ACCESS IN THE SAME CACHE INTERVAL	AT A CLEARING BOUNDARY
Returns a value or empty array	Same cached value object.	Entry removed. Next lookup runs the factory.
Returns undefined	Cached hit; no factory rerun.	Entry removed.
Returns a rejected promise	Same promise, same rejection.	Entry removed; old promise is not cancelled.
Throws synchronously	Factory runs again.	No failed entry was inserted.
Old promise settles after a new turn	It can settle for its original holders. It cannot overwrite the new entry: the scope has no settlement callback that writes to the Map.

The identity promise belongs to the cached query layer. Public findReferences awaits location data and constructs reference results again. Position definitions cache locations, then return a newly built node array on each access. These projections remain in TypeScript.

headings.text: Scope semantic caches to one turn

Six trays.
One closing routine.

Six stores stay separate.
Their lifetime gets one owner.
Every decision to carry forward
Core owns lifetime; TypeScript keeps query algorithms.
Keep one scope with six isolated handles.
Preserve exact cached values, including empty results and undefined.
Retry synchronous throws; retain rejected promises for the turn.
Begin a turn only after a successful refresh.
Clear synchronously before awaiting project release.
Extend the backend’s completion and failure boundary.
Expose the scope API; narrow beginTurn to a file list.
Clear entries without revoking handles or cancelling work.
Add ten characterization tests; retain the five existing cases.

The service chooses the stores.
The scope clears them together.
The six compartments

Two moments can empty the stores.
Only one boundary now waits longer.
Successful refresh opens the next cache interval
Release clears now and waits afterward
Scrub the release boundary
BASE
HEAD

A promise is the cached value.
The scope never waits for it.
Key is already present
Key is absent

the rationale leaves open.
